parts.text:
32 Electrons move in a vacuum from one metal plate to another metal plate. As a result of this, there
is an electric current of 48 µA between the two plates.
How many electrons are emitted by the first plate in a time of 5.0 minutes?
A
1.4 × 104
B
1.5 × 1015
C
1.8 × 1016
D
9.0 × 1016

hints: Notice the current is $48 \, \mu\text{A} = 48 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{A}$ and the time is $5.0$ minutes, so convert the time to $300 \, \text{s}$ before using $I = Q/t$.
Recall that current is rate of flow of charge, $Q = It$, and each electron carries magnitude $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$, so $Q = ne$.
First calculate $Q$ in coulombs from $48 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{A}$ times $300 \, \text{s}$, then divide that $Q$ by $1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$ to get $n$.
walkthrough: Identify the givens: $I = 48 \, \mu\text{A} = 48 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{A}$ between the plates and $t = 5.0$ minutes $= 5.0 \times 60 = 300 \, \text{s}$.
Use the definition of current $I = Q/t$ rearranged to $Q = It$ to find the total charge transferred in that time.
Relate total charge to number of electrons with $Q = ne$, where $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$, so $n = Q/e$.

A.explanation: Far too small for a $48 \, \mu\text{A}$ current for minutes. It is close to the number of microcoulombs if unit conversion and division by $e$ are missed.

B.explanation: This is the result if time is left as $5.0$ minutes instead of $300 \, \text{s}$ in $Q = It$, giving a charge and electron number $60$ times too small.

C.explanation: This is the result for a time of only $60 \, \text{s}$, one minute, instead of $5.0$ minutes $= 300 \, \text{s}$, so it is $5$ times too small.

D.explanation: Total charge $Q = It = 0.0144 \, \text{C}$ divided by $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$ gives $9.0 \times 10^{16}$ electrons.
